Why I stopped using a standing desk

I bought the thing in a burst of optimism, the way one buys running shoes in January. For a while it worked exactly as advertised: I stood, I felt virtuous, my back stopped complaining during the long afternoon stretch.

Then the novelty wore off and I noticed something the ergonomics literature had been telling me all along, which is that the posture you hold for six hours matters far less than whether you change it at all. Standing badly is not obviously better than sitting badly.

So the desk went back down, and I bought a kitchen timer instead. It cost eleven euros and has done more for my back than eight hundred euros of motorised furniture.
